scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: PC0 (20.1.1.x, on the OSPF side) reports it cannot reach
PC12 (120.1.1.x, on the EIGRP side) across the core -- they suspect the OSPF-to-
EIGRP redistribution at R11 broke, or that an interior link on the path is down.
Please confirm the cross-core fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported cross-core fault — PC0 (20.1.1.10) unable to reach PC12 (120.1.1.10)
— does not exist. Direct ping tests in both directions confirmed 5/5 packet
delivery with 0% loss and TTL=61, corresponding to exactly three router hops
(PC0 → R1 → R11 → R12 → PC12 and the symmetric return), which matches the
expected forwarding path through the OSPF/EIGRP boundary at R11.

All routing subsystems are healthy. The OSPF adjacency between R11 and R1 is
Full/DR with one stable neighbour. Both EIGRP adjacencies from R11 (to R12 on
segment EE and to R13 on segment FF) are up with active hold timers. The
EIGRP-to-OSPF direction of redistribution at R11 is fully operational: R11 is
operating as an ASBR and is flooding 11 AS-external LSAs covering all EIGRP
prefixes (102.1.x/24, 103.0.0.0/8, 112.0.0.0/8, 113.1.x/24, 120.0.0.0/8) into
the OSPF domain; R1 correctly installs 120.0.0.0/8 via OSPF. The OSPF-to-EIGRP
direction (redistribute ospf in R11's EIGRP stanza) produces no explicit entries
in R11's EIGRP topology table, but R12 and R13 both carry static kernel default
routes toward R11 (112.1.1.1 and 103.1.1.1 respectively), which provide
equivalent reachability to the entire OSPF domain without requiring per-prefix
EIGRP redistribution. No interfaces are down, no routes are missing, and there is
no black hole on any segment of the path. The helpdesk ticket describes a fault
that is not reproducible; the network is operating correctly.

Corrective action: none required. Close ticket as no-fault.
